precepts.text: That's why the Lord said, put ye no trust in a brother, for every brother will utterly supplant.
precepts.point: Some people are in your life for blessings, some in your life for cursings; but ultimately it's to try us, and try each and every one of us.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
The man of God out of Judah was charged by the word of the Lord, “Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.” The Lord told him what not to do and what to do. He refused the king, even for half his house. Then an old prophet in Bethel came after him: “I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.”

This dude was lying. God said the only one he speaks with mouth to mouth is Moses; everybody else he speaks to with dreams and visions, and this man said an angel came to him. The man of God went back, ate and drank, and “a lion met him by the way, and slew him”: “It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord”.

That is why the Lord said, “Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” That is why you have to be mindful with brothers. If God tells you something, follow it; don’t go to the left or right of what he says because a brother says so. Follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.

Some people are in your life for blessings, some are in your life for cursings; but ultimately it is to try us, each and every one of us.

precepts.text: The test of a true prophet is that the thing he speaks in the name of the Most High comes to pass.
precepts.point: He gives a sign: the altar will be rent and its ashes poured out. When Jeroboam stretches out his hand to have him seized, that hand dries up and cannot be pulled back, and the altar is rent as the sign declared.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

precepts.why:
“But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.” And how shall we know? “When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken”. The test of a true prophet is that the thing he speaks in the name of the Most High comes to pass.

The man of God out of Judah passed that test. He cried against Jeroboam's altar in Bethel that a child of the house of David, “Josiah by name”, would offer the priests of the high places upon it, “and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.” He gave a sign the same day: “Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.”

When Jeroboam put forth his hand, saying, “Lay hold on him”, his hand “dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.” “The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.” It came to pass, so the word was from the Most High.

precepts.point: The old prophet claims an angel spoke to him by the word of the Most High telling him to bring the man back, but the scripture plainly states he lied. The man of God, giving reverence to the older prophet, goes back and eats.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

precepts.why:
“Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.”

The man of God had his charge: “Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.” He repeated it to the old prophet of Bethel who rode after him and found him “sitting under an oak”. But the old prophet said, “I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water.” The scripture plainly states it: “But he lied unto him.”

The man of God gave reverence to the older prophet, and “he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.” He let the reverence of a man cause him to fall.

precepts.text: With the Most High is strength and wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are His.
precepts.point: The Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man would keep the charge, and disobedience under that dispensation carried the penalty of death.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

precepts.why:
“With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” The old prophet who lied and the man of God who was lied to were both in the hand of the Most High.

That is why the word of the Lord could come through the very prophet who had deceived him, as they sat at the table: “thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.” The Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man of God would keep the charge he had been given, “Eat no bread, and drink no water.”

He did not keep it, and under that dispensation disobedience carried the penalty of death. A lion met him by the way and slew him, and his carcase was cast in the road with the ass and the lion standing by it, neither eaten nor torn. Deceiver and deceived were both his, and the judgment was his.

precepts.text: The man of God cried against the altar of Bethel that a child named Josiah would be born to David's house and offer the priests of the high places upon it, and burn men's bones on it.
precepts.point: When told which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who prophesied these things, he said to let him alone and let no man move his bones.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
The man of God “cried against the altar in the word of the Lord, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the Lord; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.”

He named Josiah before he was born. Now Josiah broke down the altar at Beth-el and the high place Jeroboam made when he set up the golden calves, burned it and stamped it small to powder. Turning himself, he spied the sepulchres, took out the bones, “and burned them upon the altar, and polluted it, according to the word of the Lord which the man of God proclaimed.”

When he learned which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things, he said, “Let him alone; let no man move his bones.”
